recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the cron call in a script that sends a notification when nightly-sync exits non-zero, optionally adding a hosted dead man's switch that the job pings on success, and skipping the Synology/Docker logging setup entirely.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to find out when `nightly-sync` dies, without reading logs — triggered by last week's four silent crashes.
labels.Deleted: A central Synology log stack (Docker, Loki/ELK-style aggregation). Nobody asked to search or aggregate logs across services; you have one job with one failure mode.
labels.Bottleneck: The script's only signal is the success email it sends at the end, so a startup crash produces no signal at all.
labels.Checked myself: Based only on what you told me — single cron job on edna, crashes before the email step, nothing else alerts today, Synology can run Docker.

note: Borderline call: it is LARGER because the reply offers two separate alerts to set up now (an exit-code failure notification and an optional hosted dead man's switch), not deferred until a later need.
